brief.subject: Canada tariff suit, Heartland profit turn, $1M card theft
brief.headline: Court challenge hits 50% Canada tariffs as Heartland posts a real Q3 profit
brief.dek: A lawsuit targets Canada tariffs, Heartland Express turns a profit, nearly $1M in cards vanish from a truck, and LTL and rail networks shift.
brief.lede: A lawsuit at the Court of International Trade challenges the 50% tariffs on Canada. Cross-border carriers should watch the case closely.

sections.heading: Canada Tariffs Face Legal Test
bullets: 50% tariffs on Canada are now challenged in a suit filed Tuesday at the Court of International Trade.
The suit claims the president overstepped by using a statute nearly 100 years old to impose them.
Cross-border carriers should treat the case as a key watch item for northbound and southbound lane volumes.

sections.heading: Heartland Express Turns the Corner
bullets: Q3 brought Heartland its first net profit since 2023 that did not lean on big equipment or terminal sales.
A large truckload carrier earning from operations is one more data point small fleets can weigh when reading the market.

sections.heading: Nearly $1M Cargo Theft in California
bullets: Nearly $1 million in trading cards disappeared from a FedEx truck outside a California grading facility.
The driver found a cargo-door lock missing, and detectives are seeking surveillance footage.
High-value, easy-to-resell loads remain prime targets, so check locks and seals at every stop.

sections.heading: Network Moves in LTL and Rail
bullets: A. Duie Pyle is adding a Cincinnati-area LTL service center and a Camp Hill, Pennsylvania warehouse.
That expansion could mean more regional LTL competition and capacity in Ohio and Pennsylvania.
CSX cut more than 100 management positions while restructuring its engineering department.
